source_text: Nec dixisset: In eo transiit mors, in quo omnes peccaverunt [n295] , sed: In eo, quod de primi hominis et de primae mulieris diabolica voluptate et carne fluxerunt; quod si pronuntiavisset, non vestrum dogma firmasset, sed omnes suas sententias subruisset Apostolus. Ergo peccantium voluntatem et peccati accusat exemplum ac per hoc vos et ratio deproeliatur et Paulus.
pass_a_gloss: Nor would he have said: In that death passed, in which all sinned, but: In that, that they flowed from the diabolical pleasure and flesh of the first human being and of the first woman; which if he had pronounced, the Apostle would not have confirmed your dogma, but would have undermined all his own sentences. He therefore accuses the will of those sinning and the example of sin and through this both reason and Paul fight you down.

lemmas.lexica: LS exemplum; Blaise Adam as example not transmitter
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: Nor would he have said, ‘Death passed on in that all sinned’ (Romans 5:12), but, ‘In that they flowed from the diabolical pleasure and flesh of the first man and first woman.’ Had he declared this, the apostle would not have established your doctrine but overthrown all his own statements. He therefore accuses sinners’ will and sin’s example. Consequently, both reason and Paul fight against you.

choices.why: Adam as example to later sinners, Julian's alternative to tradux.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
